<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py from `liya --help`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every command accepts `-o table|json|yaml` and `--env NAME` / `--url URL`, before or
after the subcommand; `-v` / `--verbose` logs each request (never headers). Exit codes:
`0` success, `1` error (message on stderr), `2` invalid input, `3` not logged in or not
permitted, `4` not found, `5` a deliberate "no" — changes pending on `apply --dry-run`, a
blocked guardrail test, an agent that declined to answer.

## `liya`

```text
usage: liya [-h] [-o {table,json,yaml}] [--env ENV] [--url URL] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
            [--no-color] [-v] [--version]
            COMMAND ...

liya — the Liyagent / TicketIQ command line. Every command calls the same REST API as
the web console.

positional arguments:
  COMMAND
    auth                log in, log out, and show who you are
    env                 manage environments (instances)
    agents              list, configure and talk to agents
    tickets             work with tickets
    triggers            schedules, webhooks and event triggers
    providers           LLM providers
    models              the model catalogue
    guardrails          input/output guardrails
    secrets             the secret vault (values are never shown)
    policies            Cedar access policies
    audit               the audit log
    budgets             spend budgets
    tenant              a tenant's solutions, and adopting legacy history into one
    connectors          ServiceNow, Jira, Teams and other connectors
    kb                  the knowledge base
    status              gateway, model chain and connector health: the command-center
                        summary
    doctor              diagnose configuration and connectivity
    apply               apply YAML resources from a file or dir
    export              export resources as YAML files (no secrets)
    run                 run a coding agent with its model calls through the AI gateway
    version             client and server version
    completion          print a shell completion script
    tiq                 run a legacy `tiq` command (ask, plan, replay, …)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o {table,json,yaml}, --output {table,json,yaml}
                        output format: table (default), json or yaml
  --env ENV             environment to use (default: the current one)
  --url URL             instance URL, overriding the environment's
  --timeout TIMEOUT     HTTP timeout in seconds
  --no-color            disable colour (same as NO_COLOR)
  -v, --verbose         log each request's method, URL, status and latency to stderr
                        (never headers or secrets); LIYA_VERBOSE=1 too
  --version             print the client version and exit

Environment: LIYA_TOKEN, LIYA_ENV, LIYA_URL, LIYA_HOME (default ~/.liya), LIYA_OUTPUT,
NO_COLOR. Run `liya COMMAND --help` for details.
```

## `liya auth`

```text
usage: liya auth [-h] SUBCOMMAND ...

log in, log out, and show who you are

positional arguments:
  SUBCOMMAND
    login     store a credential for the current environment
    logout    forget the current environment's credential
    status    show who you are signed in as (never the token)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

### `liya auth login`

```text
usage: liya auth login [-h] [-o {table,json,yaml}] [--env ENV] [--url URL]
                       [--username USERNAME] [--token-stdin] [--password-stdin]

Log in to the current environment. Uses the server's device-code flow when it offers
one; otherwise reads LIYA_TOKEN, a token from stdin (--token-stdin), or a hidden
prompt. --username signs in with a password (hidden prompt) and stores the resulting
session, never the password. Service-account tokens (svc/NAME:SECRET) are accepted.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o {table,json,yaml}, --output {table,json,yaml}
                        output format: table (default), json or yaml
  --env ENV             environment to use
  --url URL             instance URL override
  --username USERNAME   sign in as this user (password prompted)
  --token-stdin         read the token from stdin
  --password-stdin      read the password from stdin (with --username)
```

```text
usage: liya auth logout [-h] [-o {table,json,yaml}] [--env ENV] [--url URL]

options:

  -o {table,json,yaml}, --output {table,json,yaml}
                        output format: table (default), json or yaml
```

### `liya agents chat`

```text
usage: liya agents chat [-h] [-o {table,json,yaml}] [--env ENV] [--url URL]
                        [--session SESSION] [--system SYSTEM] [--ticket TICKET]

  --env ENV             environment to use

  --ticket TICKET       ground the turn on this ticket id
```

```text
                        [--dataset DATASET] [--baseline BASELINE] [--wait WAIT]
```

```text
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o {table,json,yaml}, --output {table,json,yaml}
                        output format: table (default), json or yaml
  --env ENV             environment to use
  --url URL             instance URL override
```

### `liya policies create`

```text
usage: liya policies create [-h] [-o {table,json,yaml}] [--env ENV] [--url URL]
                            --agent AGENT --template
                            {full,read_only,readonly,sandboxed,standard}
                            [--principal PRINCIPAL] [--agent-tools] [--about ABOUT]
                            [--dry-run] [--reason REASON] [-y]
                            name

Bind a built-in template to an agent. A template is what PEOPLE may do with the agent:
readonly (read it), sandboxed (read and run it), standard (run and reconfigure it),
full (everything, the kill switch too). --principal names who (default: anyone). The
moment a policy names the agent it is governed: people without a permit lose what
their roles gave them. The agent's OWN tool and model calls are a separate decision;
--agent-tools writes them as the template implies — readonly and sandboxed: no tools
of its attached MCP servers; standard: their tools; full: those and its bound LLM
provider. Each policy is analysed first and a lockout, or one that takes a server from
another agent, is refused without --yes. --dry-run exits 5.

positional arguments:
  name                  policy name (lowercase letters, digits and -)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o {table,json,yaml}, --output {table,json,yaml}
                        output format: table (default), json or yaml
  --env ENV             environment to use
  --url URL             instance URL override
  --agent AGENT         the agent the template is bound to
  --template {full,read_only,readonly,sandboxed,standard}
                        readonly, sandboxed, standard or full
  --principal PRINCIPAL
                        any (default), user:NAME, group:NAME or role:NAME
  --agent-tools         also write the agent's own call_tool (and, for full,
                        call_model) policies the template implies
  --about ABOUT
  --dry-run             show the policies and their impact
  --reason REASON
  -y, --yes             create even where the analysis warns
```

```text
usage: liya policies apply [-h] [-o {table,json,yaml}] [--env ENV] [--url URL] -f FILE
                           [--dry-run] [--reason REASON]

options:
```

### `liya tenant solutions set`

```text
usage: liya tenant solutions set [-h] [-o {table,json,yaml}] [--env ENV] [--url URL]
                                 [--default] [--plan PLAN] [--dry-run]
                                 [--reason REASON]
                                 tenant [SOLUTION ...]

Set exactly which solutions a tenant has (instance owners only). SOLUTIONS are keys:
itsm, sap, hr, finance, and SAP's modules sap.s4, sap.sf, sap.fsm (sap alone means all
of them). --default removes the row, so the tenant falls back to the instance's — or,
with none, every GA solution. Audited as tenant.solutions.update.

positional arguments:
  tenant                tenant id, or '' for the instance
  SOLUTION

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o {table,json,yaml}, --output {table,json,yaml}
                        output format: table (default), json or yaml
  --env ENV             environment to use
  --url URL             instance URL override
  --default             remove the row instead
  --plan PLAN           a plan (starter, business, enterprise); the row grants its
                        solutions plus SOLUTIONS
  --dry-run             show what would turn on and off; write nothing
  --reason REASON       why (kept on the row and the audit log; required when anything
                        turns off)
```

### `liya tenant solutions infer`

```text
usage: liya tenant solutions infer [-h] [-o {table,json,yaml}] [--env ENV] [--url URL]
                                   [--apply]

Propose each tenant's solutions from what it uses: intake sources (itsm), SAP
connectors bound to it (sap and modules), HR switched on or HR systems bound (hr),
finance connectors (finance). A dry run unless --apply. Never proposes turning off
what is in use: a solution kept only by a shared, unbound server stays on and is
listed as ambiguous.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o {table,json,yaml}, --output {table,json,yaml}
                        output format: table (default), json or yaml
  --env ENV             environment to use
  --url URL             instance URL override
  --apply               write each proposal (audited, reason 'migration infer')
```

### `liya tenant adopt-legacy`

```text
usage: liya tenant adopt-legacy [-h] [-o {table,json,yaml}] [--env ENV] [--url URL]
                                --tenant TENANT [--dry-run] [--reason REASON]
                                [--triggers {doors,all,none}] [--no-grant-users]
                                [--no-sources]

Adopt the records written before this instance had tenants (transcripts, sessions,
answer records, trigger runs, memory, SAP/HR records; audit rows by cut-off) into
TENANT, bind the unbound door triggers and the deflection door to it and grant it to
every non-owner account that holds no tenant — so the people who used the instance
keep reading their own history, and only it. Idempotent; audited as
tenant.legacy.adopt. Run with --dry-run first.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o {table,json,yaml}, --output {table,json,yaml}
                        output format: table (default), json or yaml
  --env ENV             environment to use
  --url URL             instance URL override
  --tenant TENANT       the home tenant (it must exist)
  --dry-run             count every step; write nothing
  --reason REASON       why (required to apply; on the audit row)
  --triggers {doors,all,none}
                        unbound triggers to bind: inbound doors (default), all, or
                        none
  --no-grant-users      do not grant the home tenant to accounts holding none
  --no-sources          do not give it the unowned sources and the unsourced intake
```

```text
usage: liya run [-h] SUBCOMMAND ...

run a coding agent with its model calls through the AI gateway

    claude    start Claude Code routed through the AI gateway
```

### `liya run claude`

```text
usage: liya run claude [-h] [-o {table,json,yaml}] [--env ENV] [--url URL]
                       [--agent AGENT] [--ttl-hours TTL_HOURS] [--token-stdin]
                       [--claude-bin CLAUDE_BIN] [--dry-run] [-y]
                       ...

Start Claude Code with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL set to this instance's Anthropic gateway
(/api/gateway/anthropic) and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN to an agent's gateway token, so
every model call is that agent's governed call: kill switch, Cedar, guardrails,
budget, audit. The token comes from LIYA_GATEWAY_TOKEN, --token-stdin, or is minted
for --agent (replacing its current token; confirmed, or --yes). A Claude Code settings
file that would send calls around the gateway — CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX, _BEDROCK,
_FOUNDRY or its own ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL — refuses the launch; the same set only in this
shell is cleared from Claude Code's environment instead. Arguments after -- go to
Claude Code; its exit status is liya's.

positional arguments:
  claude_args           arguments for Claude Code, after --

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o {table,json,yaml}, --output {table,json,yaml}
                        output format: table (default), json or yaml
  --env ENV             environment to use
  --url URL             instance URL override
  --agent AGENT         mint a gateway token for this agent
  --ttl-hours TTL_HOURS
                        lifetime of a minted token (default 8)
  --token-stdin         read the agent's gateway token from stdin
  --claude-bin CLAUDE_BIN
                        the Claude Code executable (default: claude on PATH)
  --dry-run             show what would run, the token masked, and start nothing
  -y, --yes             mint without asking
```

## `liya tiq`

Forwards to the legacy `tiq` command line (`ask`, `usage`, `plan`, `policy`, `network`, `trigger`, `eval`, `agent`, `replay`, `delete`) with liya's environment and stored credential. Those verbs also work directly: `liya plan -f bundle.json`.
